title.narrative: Tanzania: Resilient Natural Resource Management for Tourism and Growth

description.narrative: The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to improve management of natural resources and tourism assets in priority areas of Southern Tanzania and to increase access to alternative livelihood activities for targeted communities

The development objective of Resilient Natural Resource Management for Tourism and Growth Project for Tanzania is to improve management of natural resources and tourism assets in priority areas of Southern Tanzania and to increase access to alternative livelihood activities for targeted communities. This project has four components. 1) The first component, Strengthen management and improve infrastructure in priority Protected Areas, has the following subcomponents: (i) Improve PA infrastructure; (ii) Strengthen management capacity and infrastructure maintenance of PAs; and (iii) Strengthen Destination Southern Tanzania. 2) The second component, Strengthen alternative livelihoods for targeted communities in proximity to the priority Protected Areas, has the following sub components: (i) Improve the governance framework of conservation-related community-based initiatives; (ii) Enhance alternative community livelihoods by improving economic opportunities and linking them with conservation of wildlife and landscapes; and (iii) Skills development for local access to jobs in tourism and conservation. 3) The third component, Strengthen landscape management and infrastructure investments in and upstream of the Ruaha National Park, has the following subcomponents: (i) Assess and implement infrastructure measures to augment dryseason flows to the RUNAPA; (ii) Improve efficiency of irrigation systems; (iii) Catchment conservation activities in selected sub-basins; and (iv) Support the consensus-building process for land and water management and climate change adaptation in the Usangu plains. 4) The fourth component, Project management, institutional strengthening, quality assurance and control, and monitoring and evaluation, aims to finance supplemental support for project management, to ensure coordinated and timely execution of infrastructure and other project activities.

condition.narrative: TANAPA appoints additional full-time staff to its environmental and social unit. TANAPA shall appoint, no later than six (6) monthsafter the Effective Date, or such other date as may be agreed with the Association, additional full-time staff to its environmentaland social management unit, in adequate numbers and with qualifications and terms of reference satisfactory to the Association, asfurther set forth in the PIM, as per section I.B.5 of the Project Agreement.

title.narrative: Households with access to alternative livelihood activities supported by the project

comment.narrative: Target 58% achieved. The indicator tracked the number of households engaged in alternative livelihood activities supported by the project, broken down by NRM (such as supply of produce and artisanal products for increased tourism, or production of higher value and less water-demanding crops), and tourism-based (through skilled and non-skilled jobs). At completion, the project supported 153 COCOBA groups from 15 priority villages ("Phase I") with grants for the implementation of productive subprojects. Source of verification: TANAPA (2024). Project Community Implementation Report.

title.narrative: Area of the priority Protected Area (PA) with improved access for basic management supported by the project

comment.narrative: Target 74% achieved. The indicator tracked improved access through the construction of roads and bridges, and new/improved infrastructure (ranger posts, entry gates, etc.) to improve basic management of the PA, namely through the maintenance of game circuit and park operations roads. At closing, key infrastructure for basic management was still undergoing construction. Source of verification: TANAPA (2024). Report on the use of REGROW project construction heavy equipment, vehicle, and tractors in Ruaha, Nyerere, Mikumi and Udzungwa National Parks.

title.narrative: Land area under sustainable landscape management practices

comment.narrative: Target 64% achieved. The indicator tracked the land area for which new and/or improved sustainable landscape management practices were introduced. At completion, the project secured 3,208 ha from watershed management activities, including tree planting, and 3,200 ha from the improvement of the Madibira irrigation scheme. Source of verification: NIRC (2024). Project Cumulative Implementation Report; RBWB (2024). Progress Implementation Report (2018-2024).

title.narrative: Total tourist visits to the priority PAs

comment.narrative: Target 79% achieved. The indicator tracked visitors paying entry fees to enter any of the priority PAs. At closing, although the rehabilitation of three airstrips, the development of the marketing strategy and the promotional efforts conducted by TTB represent valuable results, the fact that most infrastructure remained unavailable for improved access and tourism makes it difficult to fully attribute this result to the project. The overall increase in tourists could also have been due to a post-COVID return to travel and the expansion of tourist facilities by private tourist operators reported during the same period. Source of verification: TANAPA (2025). Tourists trends in Mikumi, Nyerere, Udzungwa and Ruaha National Parks.

title.narrative: Visitor information centers constructed and operational in priority Protected Areas

comment.narrative: Target not achieved. This indicator tracked the number of visitor information centers constructed and operational (staffed, equipped, and in use). At the time of the ICR mission (March 2025), two visitor information centers were undergoing construction (one in Mikumi and one in Ruaha) with an average completion rate of 82.5%. Source of verification: works progress reports; ICR mission (March 2025).

title.narrative: Destination management partnership for Southern Tanzania operational

comment.narrative: Target achieved. The indicator tracked the tourism promotion partnership between TTB, relevant private sector, TAWA, TANAPA, NGOs, and communities, operational through regular regional meetings to be held, annual work plan developed and implemented, and promotion familiarization trips conducted, etc. At project closing, 200 tourism stakeholders were engaged through familiarization trips as well as domestic and international exhibitions. Source of verification: TTB (2025). Cultural Tourism Enterprises Engagement in Southern Tanzania; TTB (2025). Participation of TTB in exhibitions under REGROW Project.

title.narrative: Ranger posts constructed or/and upgraded in priority Protected Areas

comment.narrative: Target not achieved. This indicator tracked the number of ranger posts constructed and/or upgraded. At the time of the ICR mission (March 2025), three ranger posts were being constructed (two in Nyerere and one in Ruaha) with an average completion rate of 82%. The initial target of 15 ranger posts was overly ambitious. During implementation, the project prioritized 3 ranger posts due to budget considerations. Source of verification: works progress reports; ICR mission (March 2025).

title.narrative: Dry season water supply sources constructed by the project in Ruaha National Park

comment.narrative: Target not achieved. The indicator tracked the construction of dry season water supply sources (structural measurements that are able to increase water availability during the dry season in Ruaha National Park). The short-term structural solutions that had been initially planned (low dam weir, water storage “charco” dams, ground water borewells) were not constructed due to concerns about their impact on river flows. As an urgent and provisional measure, the project excavated a total of 42 sand dams for wildlife within a 167km stretch of the Great Ruaha River in Ruaha National Park. Other structural solutions to increase dry season water supply for animals had been identified; however, these could not be completed before project closing. Source of verification: TANAPA (2024). Report on the use of REGROW project construction heavy equipment, vehicle, and tractors in Ruaha, Nyerere, Mikumi and Udzungwa National Parks.

title.narrative: Access roads rehabilitated inside priority Protected Areas

comment.narrative: Target 172% achieved. The indicator tracked both the access roads rehabilitated and new access roads constructed by the project. Even though the target was over-achieved, the key investment for constructing 1,259 km of new roads and the construction of bridges initially planned was cancelled due to budgeted considerations, limiting the presence and/or access of park staff and management for monitoring and surveillance of remote areas within the PAs. Source of verification: TANAPA (2024). Report on the use of REGROW project construction heavy equipment, vehicle, and tractors in Ruaha, Nyerere, Mikumi and Udzungwa National Parks.

title.narrative: Scholarships for vocational training in nature conservation and/or tourism hospitality awarded (disaggregated by sex, age (16-29))

comment.narrative: Target 656% achieved. The indicator tracked the scholarships for vocational training in nature conservation and/or tourism hospitality awarded. Source of verification: TANAPA (2024). Project Community Implementation Report.

title.narrative: Wildlife census conducted in priority Protected Areas

comment.narrative: Target 92% achieved. The indicator tracked the production of censuses of elephants, rhinos, and big cat populations. At completion, the following wildlife research had been conducted: (i) two technical reports; (ii) two draft manuscripts submitted to peer reviewed journals; (iii) one draft policy brief; (iv) two wildlife census; and (v) specific research on control of invasive species and relevant wildlife diseases, and collection of dry and wet season data. Source of verification: TAWA final report and copies of the research conducted.

title.narrative: Households trained by the project in alternative livelihood activities (disaggregated by sex, age (16-29))

comment.narrative: Target 67% achieved. This indicator tracked the number of households trained in alternatively livelihoods activities; namely, on COCOBA and management of community livelihood sub-projects. At project completion, the beneficiaries were from all 61 priority villages targeted by the project. Source of verification: TANAPA (2024). Project Community Implementation Report.

title.narrative: Smallholder farmers trained on the irrigation water use efficient technologies for improving farming and exploitation of water resources

comment.narrative: Target 8% achieved. The indicator tracked the training provided to farmers on efficient water use and management of irrigation schemes. At project completion, the training reached 15,390 farmers in 11 irrigator organizations. Source of verification: NIRC (2024). Project Cumulative Implementation Report.

title.narrative: Airstrips rehabilitated in selected project sites

comment.narrative: Target 20% achieved. The indicator tracked the number of airstrips rehabilitated by the project. At completion, three airstrips had been rehabilitated through works performed by the heavy machinery provided by the project to TANAPA (in each of Nyerere, Mikumi, and Ruaha National Parks). Four airstrips being rehabilitated/upgraded through contractors were still ongoing at the time of the ICR mission in March 2025. The initial target of 15 airstrips was overly ambitious and not sufficiently justified. During implementation, the project prioritized seven airstrips and these were deemed adequate for the needs of the National Parks. Source of verification: works progress reports; ICR mission (March 2025).

title.narrative: Operational water user associations and irrigators organizations strengthened under the project

comment.narrative: Target 188% achieved. The indicator tracked the number of operational water user associations and irrigator organizations strengthened under the project. At project completion, 11 IOs were trained on organization and financial management and 19 WUAs were trained on water resources and environmental conservation. Source of verification: NIRC (2024). Project Cumulative Implementation Report; RBWB (2024). Progress Implementation Reports (2018-2024).

title.narrative: Smallholder agriculture area benefiting from improved irrigation infrastructure

comment.narrative: Target 145% achieved. The indicator tracked the construction of improved irrigation infrastructure (meaning with lining and intact structures). At project completion, the rehabilitation of canals in the Madibira irrigation scheme impacted 3,200 ha (1,600 ha on each side of the lined canal). Source of verification: NIRC (2024). Project Cumulative Implementation Report.

title.narrative: Communities using project-promoted techniques to reduce human-wildlife conflict disaggregated by crop-protection and livestock-protection technique

comment.narrative: Target 14% achieved. The indicator tracked the communities (group of households) that jointly implemented techniques promoted by the project to reduce human-wildlife conflict. In one village (Kwalukwambe), crop raiding incidents were reduced from 292 in 2021 to 0 in 2023. Source of verification: TAWIRI (2024). TAWIRI Implementation Report (2018-2024).

title.narrative: Households trained by the project in reduction of human-wildlife conflicts

comment.narrative: Target 13% achieved. The indicator tracked the provision of training in reduction of human-wildlife conflicts. At project completion, a total of 380 households were involved during experimental surveys to establish non-lethal elephant mitigation methods in Iringa and Morogoro, as well as 409 Village Game Scouts from villages adjacent to the PAs. Source of verification: TAWIRI (2024). TAWIRI Implementation Report (2018-2024).

title.narrative: Product and Market Development Strategy for Southern Tanzania is developed

comment.narrative: Target achieved. The indicator tracked the development of a Product and Market Development Strategy for Southern Tanzania. Source of verification: TTB (2021). Tanzania's Southern Circuit Marketing and Promotion Strategy 2021-2026.

comment.narrative: Biannual Targets. Perception survey will focus on the interlinked aspects of livelihoods, environmental protection, social inclusion and water resources management. It captures demand-side social accountability, citizen engagement, and both natural resource managements and tourism from the perspective of target beneficiaries.
